Application dockets resolve in days; a freshness check at forward provisioning would prevent this shape.

codex-baseline's staged retrieval_log.json records result_capture_coverage 1.0 but only three calls across a ten-second span (two statpack reads and one redacted credential-shaped 'other' row), while that candidate's own retrieval.md reports reading five docket-linked Supreme Court filing PDFs and making one rate-limited CourtListener MCP search. All three candidates independently noticed this. Prediction-time and resolution-time counts are consistent with each other, so the amicus-increment claim resolves coherently, but the signal understates amicus participation by half on this case.

gaps.label: A candidate's factual premise that the docket text does not disclose (here, which side the government's response took) can only be checked through another candidate's primary-source read or an outside fetch; a provisioned text of the government response alongside the application would have settled it from the record.

A candidate's own flags.json is not staged (by design), but where it reports a data-quality problem that the evaluator's view contradicts, there is no structured way to link the two; a flag naming the alias is the workaround.
A committed indicator of which docket-entry captions the interim amicus counter matches would have made the 6-vs-13 discrepancy checkable without re-deriving it from the snapshot text.

A committed record of the disposing order's text (the per curiam and the noted dissent) would let an evaluator confirm vote and writing details on an interim cell without leaving the checkout; today only the docket entry's summary line is in the snapshot.

A conditioned interim cut by applicant class (government vs other) would let an evaluator judge the largest adjustment all three candidates made against a committed number instead of general knowledge
A per-call cutoff comparison flag in retrieval_log.json (doc date vs the prediction's frozen cutoff) would save each evaluator re-deriving it
A per-call result_capture rate varies a lot by engine (one candidate's log was entirely 'unobserved'), which limits how much a leakage grade can rest on the log rather than the candidate's own prose

A per-candidate capture-coverage summary beside the staged log (calls captured vs. calls the engine made) would make it easier to distinguish a sparse log from a genuinely quiet cell; one candidate's disclosed retrieval is largely absent from its captured log.
A stamped copy of the outcome's resolution timestamp beside each candidate's created_at would make the forward-mode sanity check one comparison instead of three file reads
A statpack cut of interim grant rate conditional on response-requested would give this moment a conditioned anchor; today the ladder columns are right-censored counts only.
